Commentary.Commentary: The ups and down of this Test have taken us on a roller coaster through the past few days. However, England weathered the stresses of the twists and turns better and have emerged with a conclusive win. This puts them at a 2-1 lead. The final Test will be held at The Oval on August 11 and gives Pakistan a chance to earn a draw. Tune in at 1530 IST as we take you through all the action. Until then, cheers and take care!

Man of the Match, Moeen Ali says that the award could have gone to a number of guys but is really pleased to be chosen. He claims to try to play the situation, doesn't like to think too much and just play the game. To him, Pakistan bowled really well and he didn't expect to play so freely but the partnership with Bairstow in the second innings was crucial. He says that he has worked on his defence and is happy about it. He adds that the breeze was really nice and that he is fortunate to have four brilliant seamers with him.

Victorious England captain, Alastair Cook says that it could be one of his best victories as his team had to fight really hard. Adds that the heavy rollers made the pitch quite flat but he thinks that his side batted really well. He says the ball got just enough reverse swing and once the bowlers got that, they have the skills, especially when enough runs are on the board. For him, 'Mo' (Moeen Ali) really tested Pakistan's technique and England are lucky they have guys who can run for 5-6 over spell stretches. He thinks the way they bowled on a flat wicket was good and the way they wiped out the deficit when they batted. To him, they opened right and all the guys stuck in. According to him, they played Yasir Shah much better because they now know how to combat that but it depends on the conditions at The Oval in the next Test.

Pakistan captain, Misbah-ul-Haq says that the game went well till the second day but started to change on day 3. Adds, Pakistan lost a couple of crucial wickets and the English openers played well. He says that his side was undisciplined and there on things didn't go their way. Credits England and says that their bowlers did really well to take out four of his main batsmen and extract reverse swing. He says that they were really competitive but the last session put them under a lot of pressure. He concedes they have a problem at The Oval as they don't have good all rounders. He is quite impressed with Sami and Azhar, who showed character and were good under pressure. It was good for him to see youngsters batting like that.

In the first innings, England could only put up a modest total of 297 after Sohail Khan's fifer. The middle order tried their best with some useful contributions from Gary Ballance and Moeen Ali. Pakistan replied strongly with the bat and got a first innings lead of 103 runs where Azhar Ali hit a magnificent ton. England came back hard in their second innings with the bat and gave a strong total for Pakistan to chase down which eventually proved enough for them to win the match and lead the series 2-1!

In the second innings, England have shown what a true team effort should look. Five of their batsmen brought in their fifties and their bowlers put in uniformly fine performances too. Their five main bowlers picked up a brace each and kept the runs down as well. Pakistan on the other hand, got off to a good start but steadily went downhill from there, with the longer formats wear and tear exposing their inconsistencies.

The final nail in the coffin came when Steven Finn claimed the wicket of Sami Aslam. Sami's was the only performance of note from the visitors as the rest of their players were not even able to make a dent in the chase. Surprisingly, the tail-enders put up a spunky fight and kept them hanging on by their fingernails but it was too many balls to last for and they finally succumbed.

Despite getting off to a shaky start, Sami Aslam and Azhar Ali provided Pakistan with a solid chance of surviving this Test. However, Moeen Ali got the breakthrough with Azhar's wicket and the visitors' middle and lower-middle order crumbled soon after. Pakistan's batsmen were unable to stand up to the combined might of the pacers.

It's been an epic journey but we have finally got the answer. It took nearly all five days but England delivered the goods on the final day to wrap up the Test. With the exception of Joe Root, who just bowled one over, each of England's bowlers picked up two wickets. At the start of the day, England continued an already healthy lead of 311 runs but put in a few more runs to give Pakistan a very challenging target of 343.

Welcome to the afternoon session. Lots to still play for. The players are out in the middle. SAMI ASLAM and AZHAR ALI to continue batting and MOEEN ALI to resume the bowling proceedings.
...Day 5, Session 2...

After their brief difficulties, it has been smooth sailing since, with Azhar Ali and Sami Aslam steadily helping ease the pressure. They are holding their nerve and are on the right track. The hosts, meanwhile, will have to find a way to break the monotony. Join us shortly for the afternoon session.

Pakistan were faced with a hard task and they didn't get off to the best of starts as struggled to score runs and negotiate the bowlers. Stuart Broad struck, taking out Mohammad Hafeez, but Azhar Ali has resuscitated their innings.

An eventful session comes to a close. England started the morning session off with a bang as Moeen Ali took Yasir Shah to the cleaners. They settled down and in the four overs they batted, took the lead to 342.
